claims.text: Adding 1–2 at.% La to a high-entropy alloy introduces lattice distortions.
La is a large-lattice-parameter element relative to the alloy constituents.
The La-induced lattice distortions scatter phonons.
Scattering by lattice distortions reduces the phonon mean free path.
The reduced phonon mean free path lowers phonon thermal conductivity.
Adding 1–2 at.% La will reduce phonon thermal conductivity by 10–20% relative to an otherwise comparable untreated alloy.
The predicted reduction applies from 300 to 1000 K.
The predicted reduction applies while the alloy remains a single-phase solid solution.
A high-entropy alloy containing 1–2 at.% La can remain in the stipulated single-phase solid-solution state.
The magnitude and applicable temperature range of the conductivity reduction may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires a 10–20% reduction, but the stated rule falsifies the hypothesis only when the reduction is below 5%. A measured reduction from 5% to less than 10% would fall outside the predicted range without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
